questions.question: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that "no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once." ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 20 (2).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Double jeopardy** means that a person cannot be prosecuted or punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• Double jeopardy is a fundamental principle of law in many countries, including the **United States and India**.
 
• The General Clauses Act of **1897** offers defense against double jeopardy as well.
 
• **Article 20(2) **of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection against double jeopardy.
 
• Article 20(2) also guarantees protection against** self-incrimination **and retroactive punishment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21(2): **

 
 
• **​**It deals with the right to life and** personal liberty**.
 
• Article 21(2) guarantees the right to a **fair trial **and due process of law.
 
 
 
• **Article 19(1):**
 
 
• It guarantees** freedom of speech**.
 
• It guarantees several other freedoms, including the **right to assemble** peacefully and the** right to practice any profession** or occupation.
 
 
 
• **Article 22(2):**
 
 
• It deals with the rights of **arrested persons.**
 
• Article 22(2) guarantees the **right to be informed **of the grounds of arrest and to consult a legal practitioner.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution states that ‘It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51 A (e)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51 A (e)** of the Constitution of India states that 'It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.'
 
• This article is part of the **Fundamental Duties** enshrined in Part IVA of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they must also be conscious of the duties they owe to their country and fellow citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and have been included to emphasize the obligations of citizens towards their nation.
 
• There are currently **eleven Fundamental Duties** listed in Article 51A of the Constitution.

questions.question: Under the discretionary power of which Article of the Indian Constitution did the SC of India recognise sex work as a profession?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 142**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 142** of the Indian Constitution **grants discretionary power to the Supreme Court of India**.
 
• This article allows the Supreme Court to pass any decree or make any order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
 
• It was under this discretionary power that the** Supreme Court of India recognized sex work as a profession**.
 
• The recognition aims to protect the rights and dignity of sex workers and to ensure their safety and well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 142** has been used in various landmark judgments to provide comprehensive justice when existing laws are inadequate.
 
• The article empowers the Supreme Court to ensure that its orders are implemented and justice is achieved, even if it means going beyond the existing legal framework.
 
• This provision underscores the role of the judiciary in upholding the principles of justice and the rule of law in India.

questions.question: In a situation wherein A (female) and B (male) are working in same office, same designation, same nature of work but unequal payment, which of the following Articles of the Constitution will be applicable?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39(d)**__

__
 
• **Article 39(d)** of the Constitution of India mandates that the state shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
 
• This article falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• The DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• Article 39(d) aims to eliminate gender discrimination in terms of wage disparity and ensure economic justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21** of the Constitution of India guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• **Article 48A** deals with the protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife.
 
• **Article 18** abolishes titles except for military and academic distinctions.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, and they aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Although not enforceable by courts, these principles are crucial for governance and are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution of India provides protection to President and Governors and Rajpramukhs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 361**__

__
 
• **Article 361** of the Constitution of India provides protection to the President and Governors and Rajpramukhs.
 
• Under this article, the President or the Governor of a state is not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office.
 
• No criminal proceedings can be initiated or continued against the President or a Governor in any court during their term of office.
 
• No process for the arrest or imprisonment of the President or a Governor can be issued from any court during their term of office.
 
• Article 361 aims to ensure the smooth functioning of the highest constitutional offices without undue legal impediments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 356** deals with the imposition of President's Rule in states under certain conditions.
 
• **Article 370** granted special autonomy to the region of Jammu and Kashmir, which has since been abrogated.
 
• **Article 352** pertains to the proclamation of emergency in the country due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• The Constitution of India, adopted on **26th November 1949** and effective from **26th January 1950**, is the longest written constitution in the world.
 
• It establishes the fundamental political principles, the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has the idea that 'No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 24 of the Indian Constitution **addresses the prohibition of child labour, aimed at **safeguarding the well-being and rights of children**.
 
• Its primary objective is to prevent the exploitation of children by prohibiting their employment in hazardous occupations or processes.
 
• According to Article 24, no child below the age of fourteen years can be employed in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment. This measure is implemented to ensure the protection of children's health, development, and access to education.
 
• While Article 24 establishes a general prohibition, it also allows for certain exceptions. These exceptions include situations where children engage in non-hazardous work within their family, participate in work as part of their school curriculum, or undertake harmless or innocent occupations.
 
• Additionally, Article 24 grants the government the authority to enact legislation specifying the occupations and processes deemed hazardous for children. This provision enables the government to establish necessary regulations and restrictions to effectively enforce the prohibition of child labour. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 22 of the Indian Constitution** addresses the protection against arrest and detention in specific circumstances. This provision applies to both citizens and non-citizens and aims to provide procedural safeguards during arrests. The fundamental principle underlying this right is to prevent arbitrary arrests and detention, ensuring that individuals are afforded due process of law.
 
• In contrast, **Article 19** safeguards six fundamental rights related to freedom, including speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• On the other hand,** Article 20** focuses on protecting citizens concerning convictions for offenses. It offers three types of protection against the State, ensuring fairness and justice in legal proceedings.

questions.question: Article 72 of the Indian constitution is related with the power of the _______ to grant pardons, etc. and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 72 of the Constitution empowers the President to grant pardons to persons who have been tried and convicted of any offence in all cases where the:

 
 
• Punishment or sentence for an offence against a Union Law.
 
• Punishment or sentence is by a court-martial (military court).
 
• Punishment is a Death sentence.​
 
 
 
• Pardoning Power of President
 
• Article 72 empowers the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence.
 
• The meaning of these terms is as follows:
 
 
• Pardon: It removes both the sentence and the conviction and completely absolves the convict from all sentences, punishments, and disqualifications.
 
• Commutation: It denotes the substitution of one form of punishment with a lighter form of punishment. For example, a death sentence may be commuted to rigorous imprisonment.
 
• Remission: It implies reducing the period of the sentence without changing its character. For example, a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for five years may be remitted to rigorous imprisonment for one year.
 
• Respite: It denotes awarding a lesser sentence in place of one originally awarded due to some special fact, such as the physical disability of a convict or the pregnancy of a woman offender.
 
• Reprieve: It implies a stay of the execution of a sentence (especially that of death) for a temporary period. Its purpose is to enable the convict to have time to seek pardon or commutation from the President.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: How many fundamental duties are set out in Part IV A (Article 51A) of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__11__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The total number of Fundamental Duties provided by **Article 51A** of the Constitution of India is **11**.
 
• **Part IVA** of the Indian Constitution deals with **Fundamental Duties**.
 
• There are** 11 Fundamental duties.**

**Article 51A:** **Fundamental duties:**

 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• To provide opportunities for education by the parent the guardian, to his child, or a ward between the age of 6-14 years as the case may be.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India provides constitutional remedies for the enforcement of fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 32**, the Constitution of India **provides constitutional remedies** for the **enforcement of fundamental rights**.
 
• Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part:
 
 
• The right to move the Supreme Court by relevant proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed.
 
• The Supreme Court shall have the power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, whichever may be appropriate, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by this Part.
 
• The right guaranteed by this article **shall not be suspended except as otherwise provided for by this Constitution**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India affirms the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred in Part III of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** gives individuals** **the **right to go to the Supreme Court directly **for the **enforcement **of the **rights conferred **in **Part III** of the Constitution.

 
 
• **Article 32 gives** the individuals the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**.
 
• It gives **individuals** the **right **to **approach **the **Supreme Court** to seek the **enforcement **of other **fundamental rights **recognised under the Constitution.
 
• The **SC **has the **power **to issue **writs **for the enforcement of any of the fundamental rights.
 
 
• The writs are viz. habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo-warranto.
 
 
 
• The **article **is **included **in **Part III **of the Constitution with **other fundamental rights**.
 
 
• The other fundamental rights are viz. Equality, Freedom of Speech and Expression, Life and Personal Liberty, and Freedom of Religion. 
 
 
 
• ** **A **person **can **approach **the Supreme Court directly** o**nly if any of these fundamental rights are violated** **under **Article 32**.
 
• The **right **to **move **the **SC **can only be **suspended **as per the **provisions provided **in the **constitution **itself. 
 
 
• As per** article 359, t**he **right to move any court** for the **enforcement **of **fundamental rights can only be suspended **during a **national emergency**.
 
 
 
• The **jurisdiction **of the **SC **is **original **but **not exclusive **when it comes to the** enforcement of fundamental rights**.
 
 
• It is to be exercised **concurrently **with the **high courts **under** Article 226**.
 
 
 
• Since the **right under Article 32** is in itself a **fundamental right**, the **availability **of **alternative remedies **is** no bar to relief **under **Article 32**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21 states **that **no person **shall be **deprived **of his **life **or **personal liberty except **according to the **procedure established **by **law**.

 
 
• The **right is available to everyone i.e. both citizens and non-citizens**.
 
• The **right to life** is not **merely confined **to **animal existence **or **survival **but also incorporates** the right to live with dignity** and all other aspects of life that makes the life meaningful, complete and worth living.
 
 
 
• **Article 37** of the **Indian Constitution **deals with the **application of the Directive Principles**.
 
 
• It states that the **provisions of** this **Part **shall not be **enforceable **by any **court**, but the **principles** are **however fundamental **in the **governance **of the **country **and the **State shall ****use **these **principles **while making **laws**.
 
• These **principles **aim to **ensure socio-economic justice **to the **people **and **establish **India as a **Welfare State**.
 
 
 
• **Article 46** states that the **State **shall **promote educational** and** economic interests** of the** weaker sections **of the people particularly that of the **Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) **and other** weaker sections**.
